questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the real difference between Bitcoin and Ethereum?
options: Ethereum has no cryptography, unlike Bitcoin
They are functionally identical
Bitcoin is programmable and Ethereum is not
Bitcoin is a currency only; Ethereum adds a programmable layer for building applications
questions.explain: Bitcoin lets you send and receive value; Ethereum takes that idea further by letting developers build smart contracts and decentralized apps on top of it.

questions.q: Who is credited, in this lesson, with the idea of a programmable blockchain?
options: Nick Szabo
Wei Dai
Vitalik Buterin
Satoshi Nakamoto
questions.explain: The lesson names Vitalik Buterin as Ethereum's creator, who came up with the idea of a programmable blockchain when developers wanted to build more than simple transactions.

questions.q: In the vending machine analogy used in this lesson, what happens if you select A4 but don't insert money?
options: Nothing about smart contracts can be explained this way
You don't get the Cheetos — the smart contract's conditions weren't met
The machine refunds double
You get the Cheetos anyway
questions.explain: A smart contract only executes when its exact conditions are met — skip a required step, like inserting payment, and nothing happens, just like the vending machine.

questions.q: Per the real flashcard definition shown in class, what does the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) actually do?
options: It replaces the need for accounts on Ethereum
It only stores Ethereum's price history
It's the decentralized runtime environment that executes smart contracts and manages the state of the Ethereum blockchain
It's a physical computer owned by Vitalik Buterin
questions.explain: The EVM ensures all nodes process the same transactions and computations in a consistent, trustless way — it's the runtime environment for smart contracts.

questions.q: What is the real difference between an externally owned account (EOA) and a smart contract account, per this lesson?
options: There is no real difference
An EOA is controlled by a private key (typically a person); a smart contract account is controlled by code
Smart contract accounts require a password instead of a private key
EOAs can execute code automatically; smart contract accounts cannot
questions.explain: An EOA is controlled by a private key and can send transactions but holds no executable code. A smart contract account is controlled by its own code and can execute functions automatically.
